concept.name: Long squeeze trading
concept.definition: Trading around the downside mirror of a short squeeze: sharp price declines that force leveraged or stop-protected long holders to sell, whose selling pressures more longs into selling and accelerates the drop. The trade either shorts into the cascade or buys the capitulation once forced selling exhausts.
concept.intuition: Crowded longs with stops at the same levels are dominoes: the first forced sales hit the next stops, and a normal dip becomes an air pocket - the squeeze trader profits from the mechanics of others' exits.
concept.mechanics: Identify crowded long positioning (high leverage, clustered stop levels, recent parabolic gains); short the breakdown through the stop cluster, or wait for the volume-spike capitulation and buy the reversion. Long squeezes are typically shorter and shallower than short squeezes because falling prices eventually meet value buyers.
concept.failure_modes: Dips driven by long liquidations are indistinguishable from the start of genuine downtrends until afterward; buying capitulation in a real repricing is catching a falling knife, and shorting the breakdown risks immediate reversion once the shallow stop pool is cleared.
concept.misconceptions: That every sharp down-move is a long squeeze to be bought; the term describes a specific forced-selling feedback loop, and without evidence of clustered leverage there is no mechanical reason to expect a bounce.
concept.example: After a vertical run, a stock breaks a level dense with retail stops and drops 4% in minutes on huge volume with no news; the squeeze buyer waits for the volume climax, enters, and exits on the 2% snapback as forced selling dries up.
